## Design

### 2026-11-04: I finished the schematic based on the split keyboard tutorial. I added the full 50 keys that I could, labeling them.

**2.3h**

I finished the schematic based on the split keyboard tutorial. I added the full 50 keys that I could, labeling them.
The labeling took a while because I was brainstorming what keys should do what. Because there's not enough keys to make a regular 75% keyboard, I had to consider using shift a long for even the letter keys to have those punctuation marks. I felt like I needed to add as many symbol marks as possible to the keyboard b/c I wanted it to be completely functional as a separate keyboard. I also kept in consideration playing games and their keybinds. I researched a bit on how to do a "game mode" for a keyboard - that's later me's coding issue.
I also added footprints based on the tutorial - I'm so glad they are sockets which makes choosing a switch less permanent. I also didn't really figure out the panelization footprint? So I'll look at it more tomorrow.

Tomorrow: finish footprints, start pcb (it's not going to be symmetrical b/c of how I type and the features I want it to have, it's gonna take a long time). Prob no silkscreen b/c it's gonna get covered by a case anyways. Speaking of cases, I'm probably going to do this: finish hardware, do coding (after setting up stuff, the logic for each key should be fairly repetitive but time-consuming), and lastly design a cool case for them (oooo I should do 2 different styles ooooo).

tldr: finished schematics, putting most of footprints in. planned out future schedule and brainstormed a lot on which key does what due to restriction on how many keys there are b/c of pins on microcontroller. super excited!!

### 2026-11-05: I paused in the middle only to realize I didn't continue... I changed so much on the pcb too...

**5.57h**

I paused in the middle only to realize I didn't continue... I changed so much on the pcb too...
Anyways, in this half hour I made a doc for more clearly understanding what each key does on each layer. I changed the pcb layout to more fit what I would actually type like. I made sure to cut the f1 and those keys so I could make control and shift their separate keys on the regular layout, and so I shifted the space bar down a "row" on the pcb but not on schematic, while I also shifted the ctrl button down which is more to my muscle memory.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/sdadIUjTGUgBWYnw4oD9AlhN8OBC1j3h/51d616047c6935295031e33f99a8a76ab1e15d532eff351b6fd68b8f089c678c.png)

So, in this big work session, I finished adding the footprints and considered heavily my budget cost, especially with microcontroller as I have a general estimate in my head of how much the custom pcb, switches, and 3dp will cost. I finished the schematics and the pcb. I initially just followed a standard keyboard setup, but starting the code (which took a while, getting repos, installing stuff and setting zmk up in github so I could work, understanding zmk), I realized that I could do much more than I thought. So, I'm deciding to add 2 layers - game layer that will be toggled with a button or hopefully a combination of buttons, and the default, good typing layer. The game layer has f1, f2, etc keys, and the space bar, ctrl, tab, and shift keys are specialized for easy of gameplay.
By reconsidering heavily the key placements, creating a google doc with the configs to be more clear, I decided to move some stuff down. In the matrix, it is connected 5x5, but on pcb, the ctrl and spacebar will be one row below everything, the place my muscle memory knows them in. Since they have dedicated keys.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/sdadIUjTGUgBWYnw4oD9AlhN8OBC1j3h/a199cc7a6ea6c1e1cd393db0b1c2926531a69bd279d0353021ce120cfb8cfb2f.png)

I initially configured everything to the previous keybinds before changing it, so next step is to check the code - is everything still referenced properly? commented/labeled properly? then I need to map keys - this will take a long time because not only do I have to learn mod-morphs and pretty tediously do all of them, but also layers and doing mod-morphs, sticky keys maybe, for both layers.

Tomorrow: check config code, map keys, commit to github (including using terminal), install firmware. Also get all parts confirmed with coupons not overlapping with other projects, so I know my budget for 3dp which will be Friday and Sunday.

tldr: finished schematics, pcbs after multiple interations and reconsiderations of keybinds (more suited towards my habits and uses). started configs of code, learned about features of zmk and adapted hardware ceiling to what I could do in code.

### 2026-11-05: ...

**6h**

...
6h work session is actually kind of crazy for me.
I don't really even remember what I did lol.
Anyways, generally, I redesigned the pcb.
Only after finishing everything, making it all pretty, did I realize that it was backwards because in order to install the key switches, the hotswap socket had to be on the back of the pcb as well as the diodes. So I flipped each footprint and rewired the entire thing. Took me a dang long time because I had to reroute stuff, but It should be fine now. I had more experience routing after the first two times I rerouted the entire thing lol.
I also coded a custom keyboard using the zmk docs. I utilized not only regular kp assignments, but also mod-morphs, hold-taps, and macros. It took a while understanding each doc for each type and implementing it with mine, and I also did a "nested" morph with the macro and a mod-morph.
I also figured out how to soft-off and turn on the keyboard without a special power button. So now any button pushed when the board is off should turn it on (have to click both sides though), and doing a certain sequence gets it turned off.
I'm pretty happy with the keybinds for now, and the pcb seems fine. The next step is to figure out the case - I have to make a top piece and bottom piece for the case and a cap over the keys so they don't get pressed and turned on randomly in my bag. But first, the case. Once I make one side, it should be easier to make the other. I just need to figure out the tolerances, screw hole sizes, top plate sizes, etc.
If I have time, I would love to customize them. I want one to be violet and black, while the other being grey and orange, so they aren't too generic.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/sdadIUjTGUgBWYnw4oD9AlhN8OBC1j3h/840c5be92c890d6e4d359a753926efff439a38ee78857bb45c98b79a15da7360.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/sdadIUjTGUgBWYnw4oD9AlhN8OBC1j3h/afb2e9f6fcf3c48720fe8c774f98423537767830239b43383943cac79fd152db.png)

Tomorrow: make the bottom part and top plate for the case (so it is functional) - figure out tolerances + switch sizes. make a decision on whether to custom the keycaps. Do ~6hrs work, wake up earlier lol. make decision on whether you're going for 3d printer b/c of time.

tldr: finished redoing the pcb b/c realized installation issues, finished writing all (I think) the custom keyboard module and installing the files (so I can just flash it on the board now), wrapped up getting hardware parts and setting tier.

### 2026-11-06: SOOOOOO 7 HR WORK DAY DANG

**7.17h**

SOOOOOO 7 HR WORK DAY DANG
I really should've done some college apps...

Okay so today I pretty much just focused on the cad. I made the basic case + designs.
Basic case:
It took a long while to understand the pcb physical spacing along with tolerances with soldering, pcb expansion/deflation during manufacturing, and pla tolerances. With my bit of experience from the project in week 2, some of the numbers were more easily recognizable and I was able to figure out the spacing from pcb top above b/c I did that similar thing during week 2. Anyways, I realized week 2 I made some mistakes but now I fixed them - especially with the 6mm wall for the keys on top.
I also designed some cool stuff - I wanted the left hand to be geometric and modern and cool, while the right side to be more sleek, firey. So, right side is orange and grey (slate grey hopefully), and left side is violet and black.
The basic case includes a bottom, spacing between bottom and pcb (to accommodate for the hot swap sockets and microcontroller usb thing, I literally just checked the dimensions as I'm writing this journal b/c I forgot if I did, it's all good) for buffer, and a spacing for pcb thickness and pcb -> top plate. The top plate is 1.5mm, it should be for mx switches. I then made the walls around the keys (18mm with 0.3mm tolerances all around) 6mm high so it will very briefly overlap the keycap (which is going to have a skirt around the switch of 1mm, I'm going to later cad it), giving it a cool look.
I finished the designs for the left side (If i don't choose to do engravings on the side of the keyboard later on in the week). I basically made the top geometric texture similar to week 2, except I also incorporated a snake design and glasses for Viper the lol player. Can you spot it? It's a little difficult to spot but I spent quite a bit of time shaping it so it is at least recognizable. I also chamfered most of the edge and fillet one edge closest to the hand and wrist so it wouldn't cut into my hand.
On the same note, on the left side I fillet the same side for my hand, but for the rest I also fillet so it's more flowy. I started to make a lotus design and a kind of ribbon around it, though I do need to fillet it down more and add more flame like sparks everywhere.
Tomorrow (though realistically Sunday because tomorrow I'm out): finish the right side design, ask for printing legion quote, shop for keyboard cases (not using hack club money, just for own benefit lol)

tldr: finished basic functionalities of keyboard casing with correct tolerances and measurements, as well as left side design. Started right side design
